name: Pirate
summary: Across Azeroth's seas, pirates prey on ships from every shore. Their crews strike Alliance, Horde, and neutral merchant vessels across the Great Sea and coastal waters. They gather under loose flags to seize wealth, cargo, and coves, sparking naval fights from Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms.

sections.title: Lords of the High Seas
sections.body: Pirate crews roam Azeroth's seas, raiding ships and coastal settlements. They are called buccaneers, corsairs, or freebooters, and nearly every race joins their ranks. Their work ranges from smuggling and kidnappings to mercenary contracts for anyone with coin. After the Third War and the collapse of northern kingdoms, naval enforcement fractured. Pirates seized the chance to build fortified footholds on neglected islands and in coastal coves.

sections.title: A Ruthless Life
sections.body: Life aboard a buccaneer vessel is brutal and often short. Crews endure squalid, rat-infested holds and harsh discipline, while supplies of limes hold scurvy at bay. Betrayal is common, and captains keep command through strength and fear of punishment. A sailor might face execution, marooning, or be fed to sharks. After battle, buccaneers celebrate with dice, song, and heavy rum.

sections.title: Factions and Havens
sections.body: Independent crews roam every sea lane, while larger organizations command enough ships to challenge sovereign navies. The Southsea Freebooters harass shipping in the waters around Kalimdor. The Bloodsail Buccaneers menace the southern seas and wage open war against the Steamwheedle Cartel in Booty Bay.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pirate, buccaneer, and freebooter?
faq.answer: Along Azeroth's sea lanes, pirate, buccaneer, and freebooter are largely interchangeable names. Some crews favor particular banners, such as the Southsea Freebooters or Bloodsail Buccaneers. All raid at sea, smuggle, rob, and plunder the coast.

faq.q: Where are the main pirate bases located?
faq.answer: Pirate crews gather in lawless anchorages and hidden harbors around the world. Their main havens include Plunder Isle and coastal camps along Tanaris, the Barrens, and Stranglethorn Vale.

Most pirate crews prey on almost anyone. They hunt merchant vessels, civilian transports, and military supply craft belonging to the Alliance, Horde, and neutral Steamwheedle Cartel. Any ship carrying gold, timber, or trade goods may draw their attack.

faq.q: How do pirate crews recruit new members?
faq.answer: Pirate crews hire desperate cutthroats and mercenaries in port towns, and they also press people into service. Captured sailors and travelers are often forced to choose between swearing fealty to the crew and being cast into the sea.

faq.q: How does Kul Tiras deal with pirates?
faq.answer: Since the Second War, Kul Tiran fleets have patrolled trade lanes, hunting pirates and marauders on the high seas.
Yes. Human crews are common, but buccaneers accept anyone willing to raid and follow orders. Their crews include orcs, goblins, trolls, and dwarves.

angles.text: Pirate crews use cutthroat tactics, blinding powder, and swift blade work, much like the practical and lethal methods favored by roguish mercenaries.
Buccaneers prowl coastal trade routes, putting Alliance transports between Stormwind, Ironforge, and Theramore under constant threat.
The Southsea Freebooters keep aggressive camps along the Durotar and Barrens coasts, raiding Horde caravans and landing parties.
Tauren traditionally dwell on the plains, but some traveling along Kalimdor's shores have ended up aboard pirate vessels, pressed into crews or seeking fortune.
